# provider

Provider contract, registry and model catalogue.

- **Runs in:** the harness process
- **Source:** [lisp/modules/harness-provider.el](../../lisp/modules/harness-provider.el)
- **Loaded:** by default
- **Requires:** nothing
- **Required by:** [agent](agent.md), [compaction](compaction.md), [cost-compare](cost-compare.md), [fallback](fallback.md), [handoff](handoff.md), [naming](naming.md), [pet](pet.md), [provider-bedrock](provider-bedrock.md), [provider-claude](provider-claude.md), [provider-copilot](provider-copilot.md), [provider-deepseek](provider-deepseek.md), [provider-demo](provider-demo.md), [provider-openai](provider-openai.md), [recap](recap.md), [tasks-search](tasks-search.md), [usage](usage.md)

## About

A provider turns a request into a stream of events (see
docs/architecture.md, "provider").  This module holds the registry,
the model catalogue and the small amount of glue that keeps every
provider honest: a request always ends with exactly one `done`
event, and callbacks never see each other's errors.

The catalogue is cached per provider.  Defining a provider again, as
every reload does, forgets that provider's models and no other's,
and the harness asks for them again on its own: `provider/model`
asks a provider whose models are not cached.  A provider that
answers at once (Claude Code's, from what its CLI last listed) has
its models found from the first lookup; nothing waits for a client
to ask `provider/models` first.  A provider that learns more later
(a new listing, the window a model really has) lists again with
`harness-provider-relist`.

No model gets a context window silently.  One its provider sizes
has that size; one it does not (a listing of bare ids, a name it
does not list) gets an estimate, flagged `:context-window-estimated`
with what it is based on in `:context-window-basis`: the same model
as another provider lists it, else the closest model of its own
provider, else the window its provider's models mostly have, else
`harness-provider-fallback-context-window`.  A provider can say
more about a name it does not list (an alias, a variant) through
its `:resolve` function.

`harness-allowed-models` keeps the harness to some models, which an
administrator's policy may set (see docs/policy.md).  Every request
for another is refused here, where every request passes, whoever
made it: a session, a task, the auto-mode judge, naming or
compaction.  The catalogue clients get (`provider/models`) lists
only the models allowed, and a tier's model is chosen among them.

## Provides

### Methods

- `provider/cache-ttl` (model-id &optional reported) — Return the seconds MODEL-ID keeps a prompt cache after its use.
- `provider/cached-models` (provider-id) — Return the models PROVIDER-ID has listed, from the cache, without waiting.
- `provider/capabilities` (model-id) — Return the capability plist for MODEL-ID.
- `provider/close` (model-id session-id) — Have MODEL-ID's provider free what it keeps for SESSION-ID: a process, say.
- `provider/complete` (request) — Start a completion for REQUEST; return a handle plist with `:cancel`.
- `provider/embed` (model-id texts &optional opts) — Return a promise of the embeddings of TEXTS, strings, by MODEL-ID.
- `provider/embeds-p` (model-id) — Non-nil when MODEL-ID's provider embeds text (see `provider/embed`).
- `provider/fit-thinking` (model-id level) — Return thinking LEVEL brought within the levels MODEL-ID offers.
- `provider/fork` (model-id state &optional checkpoint) — Ask MODEL-ID's provider to fork provider STATE.
- `provider/list` — Return registered providers as (:id :label :doc :capabilities :tiers) plists.
- `provider/model` (model-id) — Return the model plist for MODEL-ID from the catalogue, or one made for it.
- `provider/model-tier` (model-id) — Return the tier of MODEL-ID within its provider.
- `provider/models` (&optional refresh) — Return a promise of every model from every provider.
- `provider/quota` (provider-id &optional refresh) — Return a promise of PROVIDER-ID's billing and quota information, or of nil.
- `provider/tier-model` (model-id &optional tier) — Return the id of the TIER model of MODEL-ID's provider, or nil.
- `provider/tier-model-async` (model-id &optional tier) — Return a promise of (MODEL . REASON) for the TIER model, waiting if need be.
- `provider/tier-model-info` (model-id &optional tier) — Return (MODEL . REASON) for the TIER model of MODEL-ID's provider.
- `provider/tier-thinking` (model-id &optional tier) — Return the thinking level MODEL-ID's provider runs its TIER model at, or nil.
- `provider/warm` (request) — Have REQUEST's provider get ready for a request like it; non-nil if it did.

### Events

- `provider/models-updated` — (MODELS) after a provider's models were cached; MODELS is the whole catalogue.
- `provider/quota-updated` — (PROVIDER-ID QUOTA) when a provider learns new billing or quota information.
- `provider/request-started` — (PROVIDER-ID REQUEST) when a completion starts.

### Options

- `harness-allowed-models` — The models the harness may use, as patterns of model ids; nil allows any.
- `harness-cache-ttl` — Seconds a provider keeps a session's prompt cache after its last use.
- `harness-cache-ttl-overrides` — Prompt cache lifetimes of particular providers or models.
- `harness-provider-fallback-context-window` — Context window, in tokens, of a model nothing else gives a size to.

## Uses

### Methods it calls

- `session/internal-finish` ([session](session.md))
- `session/internal-start` ([session](session.md)), when it is loaded
- `session/usage-add` ([session](session.md))

### Events it emits

- `provider/models-updated`
- `provider/request-started`
